result.title: CARTA: Self-Supervised Reusable Transaction Embeddings via Heterogeneous Tokenization and Cross-Attention
result.comment: 9 pages, 4 figures. Accepted at ICAIF '26 (7th ACM International Conference on AI in Finance), Milan, Italy, November 14-17, 2026
result.summary: Acquiring fraud labels for payment transactions is expensive and inconsistent across tasks, and high-cardinality identifiers such as merchant names make one-hot feature pipelines infeasible at scale. We present CARTA, a self-supervised encoder that learns a compact 16-dim embedding from raw transactions without labels; the frozen embedding is then reused for label-efficient fraud probing and exploratory unsupervised risk stratification without retraining the encoder. CARTA uses type-specific projections with learned embedding tables for high-cardinality identifiers, trained with token excision and InfoNCE contrastive loss. On IEEE-CIS, its linear probe at 1% of labels exceeds a raw-feature probe at 100%; on IBM TabFormer (2M rows), its frozen embedding reaches GBDT AUPRC 0.508, above frequency encoding (0.411) and the merchant-dropping baseline (0.022), though fully-supervised CatBoost is stronger. CARTA is a label-free, reusable representation that complements task-specific supervised models.

AI.brief_summary: CARTA 面向支付交易的欺诈检测，用类型特定投影与高频标识符嵌入表、token excision 与 InfoNCE 对比损失，自监督学习 16 维可复用的交易嵌入，供少量标签探测和无监督风险分层使用。
AI.relevance_reason: 属金融风控表格数据的自监督表征工作，无视觉输入、无推理状态或证据筛选问题；「heterogeneous tokenization」指高基数类目标识符而非视觉 token，与 LVR/VLM 推理缺乏可核查的状态、训练或决策联系，故排除。
